holidays.name: National Chocolate Milkshake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the thick, frosty, chocolate-packed treat that has been cooling off sweet-toothed people for generations. Grab a straw and a tall glass, and add whipped cream and a cherry if you like. Nobody will judge.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on the food-holiday calendar, and diners, ice cream shops and home blenders all take part.
holidays.funFact: Early milkshakes in the 1880s were not the creamy treats we know today. They were often an alcoholic, eggnog-style drink, and the ice cream version only took off in the early 1900s.

holidays.name: National Video Games Day
holidays.description: A day for pressing start, whether you like retro arcade classics, cozy farming sims or heated online battles. It's a good excuse to dust off an old console, finally start the game in your backlog, or challenge a friend to a rematch.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It grew out of gaming culture's wish to have its own day on the calendar.
holidays.funFact: The 1958 game Tennis for Two was played on an oscilloscope. It is often called one of the earliest video games, and it was built for a science lab open house.

holidays.name: National Day of Encouragement
holidays.description: A day for lifting each other up. Send a pep-talk text, leave a kind note on a coworker's desk, or cheer on a friend who is chasing a big goal. The idea is that a few kind words can change someone's whole day.
holidays.origin: This day was created to promote the power of positive words and support. It has been observed on September 12 in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists note that praising effort rather than talent is more likely to help people keep going when things get tough.
